title: Signals & Levers • Elisabeth Hendrickson, Joel Tosi & Charles Humble • GOTO 2026

segments.text: Hello and welcome to this episode of the
go-to book club. I'm Charles Humble and
I'm joined today by Elizabeth
Hendrickson and Joel Tossy to discuss
their new book signals and levers which
is forthcoming from IT Revolution in
September. Last time Elizabeth and I
were on a goate podcast. It was go too
unscripted. And together we managed to
produce an episode that somehow has been
by a long way the most viewed and
watched and listened to thing I have
ever recorded on anything. It's not even
close. So unfortunately for me, the bar
for this episode's been set pretty high.
But I think that's down to the guest
because Elizabeth is brilliant. She
works with technical leaders and teams
to improve collaboration, tighten
feedback loops, make better decisions,
shape culture intentionally, and deliver
value predictably and sustainably. She's
one of my absolute favorite thinkers and
it was lovely to interview her last
time. We were just chatting before we
started recording and it was great fun
and I devoured this new book with real
real joy and I'm very very much looking
forward to talking to her about it
today. We're also joined by the
co-author on this book Joel. He is as
well as the co-author of this book the
co-author of coaching for learning and
creating your dojo. Joel helps
organizations through learning. This
combines a blend of systems thinking,
XP, agile, lean, DevOps, and product
thinking practices, all to embrace
learning in the context of work. Welcome
both of you to the show. It's really
lovely to be doing this.
>> So good to be here. Thank you so much.
>> Thanks for having us.
>> Absolute pleasure. So I was thinking
about my own kind of exposure to systems

more or less date it to about 2003 I

trying to build up like a mental model

that really really helped.
This may be a bit of confirmation bias

having a bit of a moment. I'm seeing

that we just got super lucky on timing.
